steps.title: Prepare buffers and reagents
steps.instruction: Make all solutions listed in the Recipes section before starting the experiment.

substeps.instruction: RIPA buffer: dissolve NaCl (150 mM), Triton X‑100 (1 % v/v), sodium deoxycholate (0.5 % w/v), Tris (50 mM, pH 8 adjusted with HCl/NaOH), EDTA (1 mM), SDS (0.1 % w/v) in water; filter‑sterilize; add 1× PIC (see below) just before use.
PIC stock: dissolve one protease‑inhibitor tablet in 1.5 mL double‑distilled H₂O to obtain a 7× stock; add 1 part stock to 6 parts RIPA to reach 1× final concentration.

5× Laemmli sample buffer: Tris (250 mM, pH 6.8 adjusted with HCl/NaOH), glycerol (50 % v/v), SDS (10 % w/v), bromophenol blue (1 % w/v); filter‑sterilize; add β‑mercaptoethanol (5 % v/v) immediately before use.
10× running buffer: Tris (250 mM), glycine (1.9 M), SDS (0.5 % w/v); autoclave.
10× transfer buffer: Tris (200 mM), glycine (1.5 M); autoclave.
PBST (1×): mix 1× PBS (pH 7) with Tween 20 to 0.1 % v/v.
Blocking buffer: combine 1× PBST with BSA to 1 % w/v.

steps.title: Dissect zebrafish eyes and freeze
steps.instruction: Place adult zebrafish in ice water (1–2 °C) for 2–5 min, decapitate, remove eyeballs with a scoop, cut the white optic nerve with micro‑scissors, then shock‑freeze 3–4 eyes per sample in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Extract proteins from eyes on ice
steps.instruction: On ice, transfer each frozen eye sample to 150 µL cold RIPA buffer containing 1× PIC, sonicate three times (3 s each at 70 % power), shake at 4 °C for 2 h, centrifuge at 5 590 × g for 30 min at 4 °C, and move the supernatant to a fresh 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Measure protein concentration with BCA assay
steps.instruction: Prepare BSA standards according to Table 1, mix 15 µL of each standard with 300 µL BCA working reagent (WR) in separate tubes, mix 300 µL of each lysate with 300 µL WR, incubate all tubes at 37 °C for 30 min, cool to room temperature, and read absorbance on a NanoDrop; calculate sample concentrations and store lysates at –80 °C if not used immediately.

substeps.instruction: BSA standard dilutions (µL of RIPA buffer / µL of stock BSA → final µg/mL): 1) 0/40 → 2000, 2) 10/30 → 1500, 3) 20/20 → 1000, 4) 20/20 (vial 2) → 750, 5) 20/20 (vial 3) → 500, 6) 30/10 (vial 5) → 125, 7) 40/0 → 0.
Prepare WR by mixing kit reagent A with reagent B at 50:1; use a sample‑to‑WR ratio of 1:20.

steps.title: Mix lysates with Laemmli loading buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1× Laemmli sample buffer containing freshly added 5 % β‑mercaptoethanol to each lysate, keep the mixture on ice.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Insert a 4–15 % Mini‑PROTEAN TGX gel into the electrophoresis cell, fill the chamber with 1× running buffer so the gel is completely covered, remove the combs, eliminate any bubbles, load 10 µL Precision Plus protein kaleidoscope marker and 20 µg of each sample, and run at approximately 100 V until the blue tracking dye reaches the bottom of the separating gel.

steps.title: Transfer proteins onto nitrocellulose membrane
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, cut a 0.45 µm nitrocellulose membrane and two filter‑paper pieces to the size of the gel, equilibrate membrane, filter paper, and two filter pads in 1× transfer buffer with 20 % MeOH in an incubator, assemble the transfer cassette (cathode → filter pad → filter paper → gel → membrane → filter paper → filter pad → anode), remove air bubbles, place the cassette in a Trans‑Blot module with an ice block and magnetic stir bar, fill the module with 1× transfer buffer containing 20 % MeOH, stir continuously, and blot at 100 V / 350 mA for ~40 min for Arr3a (≈41 kDa) or ~1 h for Grk7a (≈63 kDa). After transfer, move the membrane to a PBS dish and mark one corner to indicate the top side.

steps.title: Block membrane and apply primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Rinse the membrane twice for 5 min with 1× PBST, block for 1 h in blocking buffer on a gentle shaker, prepare primary‑antibody mix in blocking buffer at 4 °C (rabbit anti‑Arr3a 1:4 000 + mouse anti‑β‑Actin 1:6 000, or rabbit anti‑Grk7a 1:3 000 + mouse anti‑β‑Actin 1:6 000), incubate the membrane overnight at 4 °C on the shaker (the primary‑antibody solution can be reused up to five times).

steps.title: Wash and apply fluorescent secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane 5 min in blocking solution at room temperature, then three times for 10 min in 1× PBST; prepare secondary antibodies (IRDye 800CW goat anti‑rabbit IgG and IRDye 680RD goat anti‑mouse IgG) at 1:20 000 in blocking buffer, incubate the membrane for 1 h on the shaker protected from light (foil or black box), and wash three times for 5 min in 1× PBST.

steps.title: Detect infrared signals on imager
steps.instruction: Clean the scanning area of the infrared imager with water, place the membrane, define the region of interest in Image Studio software, scan, acquiring images at 700 nm for Arr3a/Grk7a and at 800 nm for β‑Actin.
